verdict.rationale: Missive's own capabilities let users act through natural language. Its in-app AI assistant runs sessions, creates drafts, answers how-to questions and composes, replies and translates. Its official MCP server lets Claude, ChatGPT or Cursor act on conversations, contacts, calendar and drafts from plain-language prompts. Coverage is not documented as complete across the product's operations, and nothing beyond vendor claims confirms it. Missing for 10: documentation that natural-language commands can drive the full range of product operations (e.g., assigning, labeling, snoozing, rules and settings) through the in-app assistant, and independent or hands-on corroboration of natural-language operation.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can operate the product with natural-language commands

citations.quote: External AI apps like Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor can now connect to Missive through the Model Context Protocol and act on your conversations, contacts, calendar, and drafts, with the permissions you choose.
Ask Claude to summarize your inbox and draft replies without leaving the chat
Long assistant sessions no longer need babysitting. The session tab now shows what the assistant is up to
Ask how a feature works, how to set up a rule, or where a setting lives. The answer comes straight from the Missive documentation instead of a guess.
Quickly compose, reply, and translate messages with AI directly in Missive.

Drafts created outside the composer, by the assistant, by a rule, or through the API and MCP server, now resolve {{ user.name }} and {{ user.email }} from your organization profile, exactly like the composer does.
